222	# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
223	# Per-function conversion
224	# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
225	
226	
227	class _Converter:
228	    def __init__(self, func: Function):
229	        self.func = func
230	        self.cfg = _CFG(func)
231	        self._fresh_counter = 0
232	
233	    def fresh(self, typ: str) -> Temp:
234	        temp = Temp(self._fresh_counter, typ)
235	        self._fresh_counter += 1
236	        return temp
237	
238	    def convert(self) -> Function:
239	        cfg = self.cfg
240	        entry = self.func.entry
241	        idom = _dominators(cfg, entry)
242	        frontiers = _dominance_frontiers(cfg, idom)
243	
244	        new_blocks = [Block(block.id) for block in cfg.blocks]
245	        block_map = dict(zip(cfg.blocks, new_blocks))
246	
247	        # -- definition sites, in original DFS definition order ----------
248	        param_temp: dict = {}
249	        defs: dict[object, list[Block]] = {}
250	        ref_order: dict[object, int] = {}
251	
252	        def register(ref, block: Block) -> None:
253	            if ref not in ref_order:
254	                ref_order[ref] = len(ref_order)
255	            defs.setdefault(ref, []).append(block)
256	
257	        for param in self.func.params:
258	            temp = self.fresh(param.slot.type)
259	            param_temp[param.slot] = temp
260	            register(param.slot, entry)
261	
262	        for block in cfg.blocks:
263	            if block not in cfg.reachable:
264	                continue
265	            for ins in block.instructions:
266	                register(ins.dest, block)
267	
268	        # -- phi placeholders at iterated dominance frontiers ------------
269	        phi_origin: dict[Phi, object] = {}
270	        block_phis: dict[Block, list[Phi]] = {}
271	        already: dict[Block, set[object]] = {
272	            block: set() for block in cfg.reachable
273	        }
274	        for ref in sorted(ref_order, key=lambda r: ref_order[r]):
275	            worklist = list(defs[ref])
276	            while worklist:
277	                site = worklist.pop()
278	                for frontier in frontiers.get(site, ()):
279	                    if ref in already[frontier]:
280	                        continue
281	                    already[frontier].add(ref)
282	                    phi = Phi(self.fresh(ref.type), {})
283	                    phi_origin[phi] = ref
284	                    block_phis.setdefault(frontier, []).append(phi)
285	                    if not any(s is frontier for s in worklist):
286	                        worklist.append(frontier)
287	
288	        for block in block_phis:
289	            block_phis[block].sort(key=lambda phi: ref_order[phi_origin[phi]])
290	
291	        # -- renaming over the dominator tree ----------------------------
292	        stacks: dict[object, list[Temp]] = {
293	            slot: [temp] for slot, temp in param_temp.items()
294	        }
295	
296	        children: dict[Block, list[Block]] = {
297	            block: [] for block in cfg.reachable
298	        }
299	        for block in cfg.sort(cfg.reachable):
300	            if block is not entry:
301	                children[idom[block]].append(block)
302	        for child_list in children.values():
303	            child_list.sort(key=lambda b: cfg.index[b])
304	
305	        def top(ref):
306	            stack = stacks.get(ref)
307	            return stack[-1] if stack else None
308	
309	        loose: dict[object, Temp] = {}
310	
311	        def use(ref):
312	            mapped = top(ref)
313	            if mapped is None:
314	                # Only reached on edges where the name is genuinely
315	                # undefined; in lowered IR such edges are unreachable, and
316	                # the placeholder disappears together with its dead phi.
317	                mapped = loose.get(ref)
318	                if mapped is None:
319	                    mapped = self.fresh(ref.type)
320	                    loose[ref] = mapped
321	            return mapped
322	
323	        def rename(old: Block, new: Block) -> None:
324	            saved = {ref: len(stack) for ref, stack in stacks.items()}
325	
326	            for phi in block_phis.get(old, ()):
327	                stacks.setdefault(phi_origin[phi], []).append(phi.dest)
328	
329	            for ins in old.instructions:
330	                if isinstance(ins, Copy):
331	                    # A copy is pure aliasing in SSA: the defined name now
332	                    # denotes the renamed source value, no instruction (and
333	                    # no fresh definition) is emitted.  This is also what
334	                    # lets branches assigning the same value share one SSA
335	                    # value and keep their merge phi trivial.
336	                    stacks.setdefault(ins.dest, []).append(use(ins.src))
337	                    continue
338	                cloned = self._clone_ins(ins, use)
339	                new.instructions.append(cloned)
340	                stacks.setdefault(ins.dest, []).append(cloned.dest)
341	
342	            new.terminator = self._clone_terminator(old.terminator,
343	                                                    block_map, use)
344	
345	            # Fill the phi of every reachable successor: current block is
346	            # the predecessor supplying top(ref) on this edge.
347	            for successor in cfg.succs[old]:
348	                if successor not in cfg.reachable:
349	                    continue
350	                for phi in block_phis.get(successor, ()):
351	                    phi.entries[new] = use(phi_origin[phi])
352	
353	            for child in children[old]:
354	                rename(child, block_map[child])
355	
356	            for ref, length in saved.items():
357	                del stacks[ref][length:]
358	
359	        rename(entry, block_map[entry])
360	
361	        for old, new in block_map.items():
362	            new.phis = list(block_phis.get(old, ()))
363	            if old not in cfg.reachable:
364	                self._clone_unreachable(old, new, block_map)
365	
366	        new_params = [
367	            Parameter(param.name, param.slot, param_temp[param.slot])
368	            for param in self.func.params
369	        ]
370	        self._prune(new_blocks)
371	        self._renumber(new_params, new_blocks)
372	
373	        return Function(
374	            self.func.name,
375	            new_params,
376	            self.func.ret_type,
377	            [],
378	            new_blocks,
379	            block_map[entry],
380	            ssa=True,
381	        )
382	
383	    # -- cloning -----------------------------------------------------------
384	
385	    def _clone_ins(self, ins, use):
386	        if isinstance(ins, Const):
387	            return Const(self.fresh(ins.dest.type), ins.value)
388	        if isinstance(ins, Copy):
389	            return Copy(self.fresh(ins.dest.type), use(ins.src))
390	        if isinstance(ins, BinOp):
391	            return BinOp(
392	                self.fresh(ins.dest.type), ins.operator,
393	                use(ins.left), use(ins.right), ins.kind, ins.type,
394	            )
395	        return Call(
396	            self.fresh(ins.dest.type), ins.name,
397	            [use(arg) for arg in ins.args], ins.type,
398	        )
399	
400	    def _clone_terminator(self, term, block_map, use):
401	        if isinstance(term, Return):
402	            return Return(None if term.value is None else use(term.value))
403	        if isinstance(term, Jump):
404	            return Jump(block_map[term.target])
405	        if isinstance(term, Branch):
406	            return Branch(
407	                use(term.cond),
408	                block_map[term.true_target],
409	                block_map[term.false_target],
410	            )
411	        return None  # pragma: no cover - lowerer always terminates blocks
412	
413	    def _clone_unreachable(self, old: Block, new: Block, block_map) -> None:
414	        """Structural clone for blocks unreachable from the entry.
415	
416	        ``lower_module`` never emits such blocks; this keeps the transform
417	        total without inserting phi nodes that no reachable edge feeds.
418	        """
419	        local: dict[object, Temp] = {}
420	
421	        def local_use(ref):
422	            mapped = local.get(ref)
423	            if mapped is None:
424	                mapped = self.fresh(ref.type)
425	                local[ref] = mapped
426	            return mapped
427	
428	        new.phis = []
429	        new.instructions = []
430	        for ins in old.instructions:
431	            if isinstance(ins, Copy):
432	                local[ins.dest] = local_use(ins.src)
433	                continue
434	            cloned = self._clone_ins(ins, local_use)
435	            local[ins.dest] = cloned.dest
436	            new.instructions.append(cloned)
437	        new.terminator = self._clone_terminator(
438	            old.terminator, block_map, local_use
439	        )
440	
441	    # -- phi pruning -------------------------------------------------------
442	
443	    def _prune(self, blocks: list[Block]) -> None:
444	        """Remove dead and trivial phi nodes to a fixpoint.
445	
446	        A phi is *dead* when nothing outside the phi-only reference graph
447	        reads its result: phi-only cycles (e.g. a loop-carried temporary
448	        nobody reads) evaporate together.  A phi is *trivial* when its
449	        incoming values collapse to one distinct value once previously
450	        removed phis are chased through; a loop self-reference on its own
451	        result counts as such.  Dead phis are dropped as a batch first,
452	        then trivial phis one at a time; the two passes alternate until
453	        neither fires.
454	        """
455	        while self._remove_dead_phis(blocks) | self._remove_trivial_phis(
456	            blocks
457	        ):
458	            pass
459	
460	    def _live_phi_dests(self, blocks: list[Block]) -> set[int]:
461	        all_phis = [phi for block in blocks for phi in block.phis]
462	
463	        # Worklist starts from temps consumed by ordinary instructions and
464	        # terminators; reaching a phi's result marks that phi live and in
465	        # turn activates the phis feeding it.  A closed phi-only cycle is
466	        # never seeded and so dies wholesale.
467	        worklist: list[int] = []
468	        for block in blocks:
469	            for ins in block.instructions:
470	                worklist.extend(id(v) for v in _operands(ins))
471	            worklist.extend(id(v) for v in _term_operands(block.terminator))
472	
473	        live: set[int] = set()
474	        phi_by_dest = {id(phi.dest): phi for phi in all_phis}
475	        while worklist:
476	            temp_id = worklist.pop()
477	            if temp_id in live:
478	                continue
479	            live.add(temp_id)
480	            phi = phi_by_dest.get(temp_id)
481	            if phi is not None:
482	                for value in phi.entries.values():
483	                    if value is not None and value is not phi.dest:
484	                        worklist.append(id(value))
485	        return live
486	
487	    def _remove_dead_phis(self, blocks: list[Block]) -> bool:
488	        live = self._live_phi_dests(blocks)
489	        changed = False
490	        for block in blocks:
491	            for phi in list(block.phis):
492	                if id(phi.dest) not in live:
493	                    block.phis.remove(phi)
494	                    changed = True
495	        return changed
496	
497	    def _remove_trivial_phis(self, blocks: list[Block]) -> bool:
498	        representative: dict[Temp, Temp] = {}
499	
500	        def canonical(value: Temp) -> Temp:
501	            seen = set()
502	            while value in representative and id(value) not in seen:
503	                seen.add(id(value))
504	                value = representative[value]
505	            return value
506	
507	        for block in blocks:
508	            for phi in list(block.phis):
509	                incoming = {
510	                    canonical(value)
511	                    for value in phi.entries.values()
512	                    if value is not None and value is not phi.dest
513	                }
514	                if len(incoming) == 1:
515	                    replacement = next(iter(incoming))
516	                    representative[phi.dest] = replacement
517	                    block.phis.remove(phi)
518	                    self._replace(blocks, phi.dest, replacement)
519	                    return True
520	        return False
521	
522	    def _replace(self, blocks: list[Block], old: Temp, new: Temp) -> None:
523	        def subst(value):
524	            return new if value is old else value
525	
526	        for block in blocks:
527	            for phi in block.phis:
528	                phi.entries = {
529	                    pred: subst(value) for pred, value in phi.entries.items()
530	                }
531	            for ins in block.instructions:
532	                _map_operands(ins, subst)
533	            _map_term_operands(block.terminator, subst)
534	
535	    # -- canonical numbering ----------------------------------------------
536	
537	    def _renumber(
538	        self, params: list[Parameter], blocks: list[Block]
539	    ) -> None:
540	        """Assign deterministic per-function SSA ids in place.
541	
542	        Parameters take ids first in parameter order; within each block
543	        (visited in id order) phi results precede ordinary instruction
544	        results.  Everything after renumbering refers to the new temps.
545	        """
546	        number: dict[Temp, Temp] = {}
547	        next_id = 0
548	
549	        def assign(temp: Temp) -> Temp:
550	            nonlocal next_id
551	            mapped = number.get(temp)
552	            if mapped is None:
553	                mapped = Temp(next_id, temp.type)
554	                next_id += 1
555	                number[temp] = mapped
556	            return mapped
557	
558	        for param in params:
559	            param.temp = assign(param.temp)
560	
561	        for block in blocks:
562	            for phi in block.phis:
563	                assign(phi.dest)
564	            for ins in block.instructions:
565	                assign(ins.dest)
566	
567	        def numbered(value):
568	            if value is None:
569	                return None
570	            mapped = number.get(value)
571	            if mapped is None:
572	                # Defensive: an operand with no reachable definition.
573	                # Never occurs for lowered, pruned IR.
574	                mapped = assign(value)
575	            return mapped
576	
577	        for block in blocks:
578	            for phi in block.phis:
579	                dest = numbered(phi.dest)
580	                phi.entries = {
581	                    pred: numbered(value)
582	                    for pred, value in sorted(
583	                        phi.entries.items(), key=lambda item: item[0].id
584	                    )
585	                }
586	                phi.dest = dest
587	            for ins in block.instructions:
588	                ins.dest = numbered(ins.dest)
589	                _map_operands(ins, numbered)
590	            _map_term_operands(block.terminator, numbered)
591	
592	
593	# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
594	# Idempotent cloning of an already-SSA module
595	# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
596	
597	
598	def _clone_ssa_module(module: Module) -> Module:
599	    return Module(
600	        [_clone_ssa_function(func) for func in module.functions], ssa=True
601	    )
602	
603	
604	def _clone_ssa_function(func: Function) -> Function:
605	    new_blocks = [Block(block.id) for block in func.blocks]
606	    block_map = dict(zip(func.blocks, new_blocks))
607	
608	    number: dict[Temp, Temp] = {}
609	    next_id = 0
610	
611	    def assign(temp: Temp) -> Temp:
612	        nonlocal next_id
613	        mapped = number.get(temp)
614	        if mapped is None:
615	            mapped = Temp(next_id, temp.type)
616	            next_id += 1
617	            number[temp] = mapped
618	        return mapped
619	
620	    new_params: list[Parameter] = []
621	    for param in func.params:
622	        new_params.append(
623	            Parameter(param.name, param.slot, assign(param.temp))
624	        )
625	    for block, new_block in zip(func.blocks, new_blocks):
626	        for phi in block.phis:
627	            assign(phi.dest)
628	        for ins in block.instructions:
629	            assign(ins.dest)
630	
631	    def ref(value):
632	        return number[value] if value is not None else None
633	
634	    for block, new_block in zip(func.blocks, new_blocks):
635	        for phi in block.phis:
636	            entries = {
637	                block_map[pred]: ref(value)
638	                for pred, value in sorted(
639	                    phi.entries.items(), key=lambda item: item[0].id
640	                )
641	            }
642	            new_block.phis.append(Phi(ref(phi.dest), entries))
643	        for ins in block.instructions:
644	            if isinstance(ins, Const):
645	                clone = Const(ref(ins.dest), ins.value)
646	            elif isinstance(ins, Copy):
647	                clone = Copy(ref(ins.dest), ref(ins.src))
648	            elif isinstance(ins, BinOp):
649	                clone = BinOp(
650	                    ref(ins.dest), ins.operator, ref(ins.left),
651	                    ref(ins.right), ins.kind, ins.type,
652	                )
653	            else:
654	                clone = Call(
655	                    ref(ins.dest), ins.name,
656	                    [ref(arg) for arg in ins.args], ins.type,
657	                )
658	            new_block.instructions.append(clone)
659	        term = block.terminator
660	        if isinstance(term, Return):
661	            new_block.terminator = Return(ref(term.value))
662	        elif isinstance(term, Jump):
663	            new_block.terminator = Jump(block_map[term.target])
664	        elif isinstance(term, Branch):
665	            new_block.terminator = Branch(
666	                ref(term.cond),
667	                block_map[term.true_target],
668	                block_map[term.false_target],
669	            )
670	
671	    return Function(
672	        func.name,
673	        new_params,
674	        func.ret_type,
675	        list(func.locals),
676	        new_blocks,
677	        block_map[func.entry],
678	        ssa=True,
679	    )
680

1	"""The control-flow IR object model.
2	
3	The IR is intentionally tiny and directly traversable::
4	
5	    Module
6	      Function            (signature, local slots, basic blocks)
7	        Block             (phi nodes, ordered instructions, one terminator)
8	          Phi             (SSA only; one incoming value per predecessor)
9	          Instruction     (Const / Copy / BinOp / Call, all write a dest)
10	          Terminator      (Return / Jump / Branch)
11	
12	Two flavors of module exist:
13	
14	* non-SSA (produced by :func:`lower_module`): value references are
15	  :class:`Temp` -- numbered temporaries produced by instructions -- and
16	  :class:`Slot`, numbered mutable local storage (parameters and ``let``
17	  variables).  Temporaries are mostly single assignment; the sole exception
18	  is the result temporary of a short-circuit boolean operation, which is
19	  written once on each participating path, as is natural in non-SSA form.
20	* SSA (produced by :func:`to_ssa`): every parameter and every instruction
21	  result is a unique definition, slots never appear, and control-flow joins
22	  carry :class:`Phi` nodes listed before the block's ordinary instructions.
23	
24	Both flavors reuse the same node classes; a module's ``ssa`` flag (and each
25	function's) says which one it is.
26	"""
27	from __future__ import annotations
28	
29	from dataclasses import dataclass, field
30	from typing import Optional, Union
31	
32	
33	@dataclass(frozen=True)
34	class Temp:
35	    id: int
36	    type: str
37	
38	    def __str__(self) -> str:
39	        return f"%t{self.id}"
40	
41	
42	@dataclass(frozen=True)
43	class Slot:
44	    """A mutable local slot (parameter or ``let`` variable)."""
45	
46	    id: int
47	    type: str
48	
49	    def __str__(self) -> str:
50	        return f"%v{self.id}"
51	
52	
53	ValueRef = Union[Temp, Slot]
54	
55	
56	@dataclass
57	class Const:
58	    dest: Temp
59	    value: Union[int, bool]
60	
61	    @property
62	    def op(self) -> str:
63	        return "const"
64	
65	
66	@dataclass
67	class Copy:
68	    dest: Union[Temp, Slot]
69	    src: ValueRef
70	
71	    @property
72	    def op(self) -> str:
73	        return "copy"
74	
75	
76	@dataclass
77	class BinOp:
78	    dest: Temp
79	    operator: str
80	    left: ValueRef
81	    right: ValueRef
82	    kind: str  # "arith" or "compare"
83	    type: str  # result type
84	
85	    @property
86	    def op(self) -> str:
87	        return self.kind
88	
89	
90	@dataclass
91	class Call:
92	    dest: Temp
93	    name: str
94	    args: list[ValueRef]
95	    type: str
96	
97	    @property
98	    def op(self) -> str:
99	        return "call"
100	
101	
102	Instruction = Union[Const, Copy, BinOp, Call]
103	
104	
105	@dataclass(eq=False)
106	class Phi:
107	    """An SSA phi function: merges definitions from predecessor blocks.
108	
109	    ``entries`` maps a predecessor :class:`Block` to the value that is live
110	    on that edge.  Entries are kept sorted by predecessor label whenever a
111	    module is emitted by :func:`to_ssa`; only reachable predecessors occur.
112	    """
113	
114	    dest: Temp
115	    entries: dict["Block", ValueRef] = field(default_factory=dict)
116	
117	    @property
118	    def op(self) -> str:
119	        return "phi"
120	
121	    @property
122	    def type(self) -> str:
123	        return self.dest.type
124	
125	
126	@dataclass
127	class Return:
128	    value: Optional[ValueRef]
129	
130	    @property
131	    def op(self) -> str:
132	        return "return"
133	
134	
135	@dataclass
136	class Jump:
137	    target: "Block"
138	
139	    @property
140	    def op(self) -> str:
141	        return "jump"
142	
143	
144	@dataclass
145	class Branch:
146	    cond: ValueRef
147	    true_target: "Block"
148	    false_target: "Block"
149	
150	    @property
151	    def op(self) -> str:
152	        return "br"
153	
154	
155	Terminator = Union[Return, Jump, Branch]
156	
157	
158	@dataclass(eq=False)
159	class Block:
160	    id: int
161	    instructions: list[Instruction] = field(default_factory=list)
162	    terminator: Optional[Terminator] = None
163	    # SSA only; empty in non-SSA blocks.  Phi nodes precede the ordinary
164	    # instructions.
165	    phis: list[Phi] = field(default_factory=list)
166	
167	    @property
168	    def label(self) -> str:
169	        return f"b{self.id}"
170	
171	    @property
172	    def is_terminated(self) -> bool:
173	        return self.terminator is not None
174	
175	
176	@dataclass
177	class Parameter:
178	    name: str
179	    slot: Slot
180	    # SSA only: the unique parameter definition.  None in non-SSA functions,
181	    # where the parameter is read through ``slot``.
182	    temp: Optional[Temp] = None
183	
184	
185	@dataclass
186	class Function:
187	    name: str
188	    params: list[Parameter]
189	    ret_type: str
190	    locals: list[Slot]
191	    blocks: list[Block]
192	    entry: Block
193	    ssa: bool = False
194	
195	    def is_void(self) -> bool:
196	        return self.ret_type == "void"
197	
198	
199	@dataclass
200	class Module:
201	    functions: list[Function]
202	    ssa: bool = False
203

"""compiler-ir: AST -> control-flow IR lowering pipeline.

Public entry points
-------------------
* :func:`lower_ir` / :func:`lower_module` -- accept a program AST made of
  plain dicts and lists, run name resolution and type checking, and return
  a traversable non-SSA :class:`Module`.
* :func:`to_ssa` -- convert a :class:`Module` into a brand new, traversable
  pruned-SSA :class:`Module` without mutating the input.
* :func:`eliminate_dead_code` -- remove definitions unreachable from the
  SSA roots (terminator operands and calls) into a brand new SSA
  :class:`Module`, without mutating the input.
* :func:`fold_constants` -- propagate known literals along SSA def-use
  chains and fold constant arithmetic/comparison BinOps and same-literal
  phis into a brand new SSA :class:`Module`, without mutating the input.
* :func:`optimize_module` -- library-level driver running an ordered
  schedule of ``to_ssa`` / ``fold_constants`` / ``eliminate_dead_code``
  (default ``ssa, fold, dce, ssa``) into a brand new SSA
  :class:`Module`, without mutating the input or rendering text.
* :func:`render_module` -- render either flavor of :class:`Module` to
  deterministic text.
* :func:`emit_ir` -- convenience wrapper combining lowering and rendering.
"""
__version__ = "0.1.0"

from .errors import (
    CompilerError,
    DuplicateSymbolError,
    InvalidAstError,
    MissingReturnError,
    TypeCheckError,
    UndefinedSymbolError,
)
from .ir_nodes import (
    BinOp,
    Block,
    Branch,
    Call,
    Const,
    Copy,
    Function,
    Jump,
    Module,
    Parameter,
    Phi,
    Return,
    Slot,
    Temp,
)
from .lowerer import lower_ir, lower_module
from .printer import render_module
from .ssa import to_ssa
from .dce import eliminate_dead_code
from .folding import fold_constants
from .pipeline import optimize_module


def emit_ir(ast: dict) -> str:
    """Validate, analyze and lower ``ast`` and return its text IR."""
    return render_module(lower_module(ast))


__all__ = [
    "__version__",
    # entry points
    "lower_ir",
    "lower_module",
    "to_ssa",
    "eliminate_dead_code",
    "fold_constants",
    "optimize_module",
    "render_module",
    "emit_ir",
    # IR object model
    "Module",
    "Function",
    "Block",
    "Parameter",
    "Phi",
    "Temp",
    "Slot",
    "Const",
    "Copy",
    "BinOp",

1	"""Library-level optimization pipeline.
2	
3	The entry point :func:`optimize_module` collects into one library function
4	the pass orchestration that callers previously hand-wrote around
5	:func:`~compiler_ir.ssa.to_ssa`,
6	:func:`~compiler_ir.folding.fold_constants` and
7	:func:`~compiler_ir.dce.eliminate_dead_code`::
8	
9	    optimized = optimize_module(module)                     # default schedule
10	    optimized = optimize_module(module, ("ssa", "fold"))   # explicit order
11	    copied    = optimize_module(module, ())                 # copy only
12	
13	The accepted inputs are exactly:
14	
15	* a non-SSA :class:`Module` produced by
16	  :func:`~compiler_ir.lowerer.lower_module`, or
17	* an existing SSA :class:`Module` (for example the result of an earlier
18	  :func:`optimize_module` call).
19	
20	``passes`` is a finite sequence of the names ``"ssa"``, ``"fold"`` and
21	``"dce"``; passes run in the given order and names may repeat (``ssa``
22	freely, and ``fold``/``dce`` whenever the SSA stage constraint holds).
23	When it is omitted, the schedule is ``("ssa", "fold", "dce", "ssa")``:
24	SSA construction, constant folding, dead-code elimination, and a trailing
25	SSA canonicalization that renumbers away the definition holes DCE may
26	leave, so the result is the fixed point of the default sequence.
27	
28	Stage constraint
29	----------------
30	
31	``fold`` and ``dce`` require an SSA module.  On a non-SSA input the first
32	such name in the sequence must be preceded by an ``ssa``; an SSA input is
33	already past that stage, so it may start directly with ``fold`` or ``dce``
34	(an explicit ``ssa`` then merely re-canonicalizes the numbering).
35	:func:`~compiler_ir.printer.render_module` is not an optimization and is
36	never part of a schedule -- it is reported as an unknown name.
37	
38	An empty sequence performs no optimization: it returns a brand new module
39	with equivalent content, preserving the input's SSA/non-SSA flavor.  No
40	schedule, including the empty one, renders text -- the result is always a
41	traversable :class:`Module` the caller may hand to
42	:func:`~compiler_ir.printer.render_module` itself.
43	
44	Every call -- even with an empty schedule, and even on the empty module --
45	returns fresh function, block, instruction and phi containers; the input
46	module is never mutated and shares no mutable container with the result.
47	
48	Validation happens *before* any pass runs.  A non-:class:`Module`
49	``module`` raises :class:`TypeError`; ``passes`` given as a single string
50	or any non-sequence, or containing non-string elements, raises
51	:class:`TypeError`; unknown pass names and ``fold``/``dce`` scheduled
52	before the first SSA stage on a non-SSA input raise :class:`ValueError`.
53	A rejected call leaves the input module unchanged.
54	"""
55	from collections.abc import Sequence
56	
57	from .dce import eliminate_dead_code
58	from .folding import fold_constants
59	from .ir_nodes import (
60	    BinOp,
61	    Block,
62	    Branch,
63	    Call,
64	    Const,
65	    Copy,
66	    Function,
67	    Jump,
68	    Module,
69	    Parameter,
70	    Phi,
71	    Return,
72	)
73	from .ssa import to_ssa
74	
75	#: Pass names that may appear in an explicit schedule.
76	PASS_NAMES = ("ssa", "fold", "dce")
77	
78	#: Schedule used when ``passes`` is omitted.
79	DEFAULT_PASSES = ("ssa", "fold", "dce", "ssa")
80	
81	_PASS_FUNCS = {
82	    "ssa": to_ssa,
83	    "fold": fold_constants,
84	    "dce": eliminate_dead_code,
85	}
86	
87	#: Names whose stage precondition is an SSA module.
88	_SSA_DEPENDENT = frozenset(("fold", "dce"))
89	
90	
91	def optimize_module(module: Module, passes=None) -> Module:
92	    """Run an ordered schedule of optimization passes over ``module``.
93	
94	    :param module: a non-SSA :class:`Module` from
95	        :func:`~compiler_ir.lowerer.lower_module` or an existing SSA
96	        :class:`Module`.
97	    :param passes: an optional finite sequence of pass names drawn from
98	        ``"ssa"``, ``"fold"`` and ``"dce"``.  When ``None`` (the default)
99	        the schedule is ``("ssa", "fold", "dce", "ssa")``.  An empty
100	        sequence returns an independent, content-equivalent copy.
101	    :return: a brand new SSA :class:`Module` for any non-empty schedule;
102	        for an empty schedule the copy keeps the input's SSA flavor.  The
103	        result is traversable and renderable, and shares no mutable
104	        container with the input.
105	    :raises TypeError: if ``module`` is not a :class:`Module`, or
106	        ``passes`` is a string, a non-sequence, or contains non-string
107	        elements.

"""Library-level optimization pipeline.

The entry point :func:`optimize_module` collects into one library function
the pass orchestration that callers previously hand-wrote around
:func:`~compiler_ir.ssa.to_ssa`,
:func:`~compiler_ir.folding.fold_constants` and
:func:`~compiler_ir.dce.eliminate_dead_code`::

    optimized = optimize_module(module)                     # default schedule
    optimized = optimize_module(module, ("ssa", "fold"))   # explicit order
    copied    = optimize_module(module, ())                 # copy only

The accepted inputs are exactly:

* a non-SSA :class:`Module` produced by
  :func:`~compiler_ir.lowerer.lower_module`, or
* an existing SSA :class:`Module` (for example the result of an earlier
  :func:`optimize_module` call).

``passes`` is a finite sequence of the names ``"ssa"``, ``"fold"`` and
``"dce"``; passes run in the given order and names may repeat (``ssa``
freely, and ``fold``/``dce`` whenever the SSA stage constraint holds).
When it is omitted, the schedule is ``("ssa", "fold", "dce", "ssa")``:
SSA construction, constant folding, dead-code elimination, and a trailing
SSA canonicalization that renumbers away the definition holes DCE may
leave, so the result is the fixed point of the default sequence.

Stage constraint
----------------

``fold`` and ``dce`` require an SSA module.  On a non-SSA input the first
such name in the sequence must be preceded by an ``ssa``; an SSA input is
already past that stage, so it may start directly with ``fold`` or ``dce``
(an explicit ``ssa`` then merely re-canonicalizes the numbering).
:func:`~compiler_ir.printer.render_module` is not an optimization and is
never part of a schedule -- it is reported as an unknown name.

An empty sequence performs no optimization: it returns a brand new module
with equivalent content, preserving the input's SSA/non-SSA flavor.  No
schedule, including the empty one, renders text -- the result is always a
traversable :class:`Module` the caller may hand to
:func:`~compiler_ir.printer.render_module` itself.

Every call -- even with an empty schedule, and even on the empty module --
returns fresh function, block, instruction and phi containers; the input
module is never mutated and shares no mutable container with the result.

Validation happens *before* any pass runs.  A non-:class:`Module`
``module`` raises :class:`TypeError`; ``passes`` given as a single string
or any non-sequence, or containing non-string elements, raises
:class:`TypeError`; unknown pass names and ``fold``/``dce`` scheduled
before the first SSA stage on a non-SSA input raise :class:`ValueError`.
A rejected call leaves the input module unchanged.
"""
from collections.abc import Sequence

from .dce import eliminate_dead_code
from .folding import fold_constants
from .ir_nodes import (
    BinOp,
    Block,
    Branch,
    Call,
    Const,
    Copy,
    Function,
    Jump,
    Module,
    Parameter,
    Phi,
    Return,
)
from .ssa import to_ssa

#: Pass names that may appear in an explicit schedule.
PASS_NAMES = ("ssa", "fold", "dce")

#: Schedule used when ``passes`` is omitted.
DEFAULT_PASSES = ("ssa", "fold", "dce", "ssa")

_PASS_FUNCS = {
    "ssa": to_ssa,
    "fold": fold_constants,
    "dce": eliminate_dead_code,
}

#: Names whose stage precondition is an SSA module.
_SSA_DEPENDENT = frozenset(("fold", "dce"))


def optimize_module(module: Module, passes=None) -> Module:
    """Run an ordered schedule of optimization passes over ``module``.

    :param module: a non-SSA :class:`Module` from
        :func:`~compiler_ir.lowerer.lower_module` or an existing SSA
        :class:`Module`.
    :param passes: an optional finite sequence of pass names drawn from
        ``"ssa"``, ``"fold"`` and ``"dce"``.  When ``None`` (the default)
        the schedule is ``("ssa", "fold", "dce", "ssa")``.  An empty
        sequence returns an independent, content-equivalent copy.
    :return: a brand new SSA :class:`Module` for any non-empty schedule;
        for an empty schedule the copy keeps the input's SSA flavor.  The
        result is traversable and renderable, and shares no mutable
        container with the input.
    :raises TypeError: if ``module`` is not a :class:`Module`, or
        ``passes`` is a string, a non-sequence, or contains non-string
        elements.
    :raises ValueError: if ``passes`` contains an unknown name (including
        ``"render_module"``), or schedules ``fold``/``dce`` on a non-SSA
        input before any ``ssa`` stage.
    """
    if not isinstance(module, Module):
        raise TypeError(
            "optimize_module expects a Module, got "
            f"{type(module).__name__}"
        )

    if passes is None:
        schedule = DEFAULT_PASSES
    else:
        schedule = _validate_passes(passes)

    if not schedule:
        # No optimization requested: return an independent copy in the
        # same flavor.  An SSA module clones through to_ssa (its documented
        # idempotent copy); a non-SSA module is structurally deep-copied so
        # slots and short-circuit temporaries keep their non-SSA semantics.
        if getattr(module, "ssa", False):
            return to_ssa(module)
        return _clone_non_ssa_module(module)

    # Up-front stage validation over the whole order, before any pass runs.
    # An SSA input starts past the SSA stage; a non-SSA input must meet its
    # first fold/dce only after an ssa entry.
    ssa_stage = bool(getattr(module, "ssa", False))
    for name in schedule:
        if name == "ssa":
            ssa_stage = True
        elif name in _SSA_DEPENDENT and not ssa_stage:
            raise ValueError(
                "pass order violates precondition: "
                f"{name!r} requires an SSA module, but no 'ssa' pass "
                "precedes it"
            )

    current = module
    for name in schedule:
        current = _PASS_FUNCS[name](current)
    return current


def _validate_passes(passes) -> tuple:
    """Validate the user-supplied schedule's shape, independent of module.

    Returns the schedule as a fresh tuple so iteration is stable and
    independent of any caller-owned container.
    """
    # A single string is the classic mistake ("passes='fold'"); reject it
    # before the Sequence membership test would otherwise iterate letters.
    if isinstance(passes, str) or not isinstance(passes, Sequence):
        raise TypeError(
            "optimize_module expects passes to be a sequence of pass name "
            f"strings or None, got {type(passes).__name__}"
        )

    schedule = tuple(passes)
    for index, name in enumerate(schedule):
        if not isinstance(name, str):
            raise TypeError(
                "optimize_module pass names must be strings; element "
                f"{index} is {type(name).__name__}"
            )
        if name not in _PASS_FUNCS:
            # render_module (and "isel", "inline", ...) is intentionally
            # not an optimizable pass: report it like any unknown name.
            raise ValueError(f"unknown pass in order: {name!r}")
    return schedule


# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Structural copy of a non-SSA module (empty-schedule path only)
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------


def _clone_non_ssa_module(module: Module) -> Module:
    """Deep-copy a non-SSA :class:`Module` with full container independence.

    Slots and temporaries are immutable value objects and may be shared
    harmlessly, while every function, block, instruction, terminator and
    parameter container is rebuilt and every terminator edge is repointed
    at the cloned block.
    """
    return Module(
        [_clone_non_ssa_function(func) for func in module.functions],
        ssa=False,
    )


def _clone_non_ssa_function(func: Function) -> Function:
    new_blocks = [Block(block.id) for block in func.blocks]
    block_map = dict(zip(func.blocks, new_blocks))

    new_params = [
        Parameter(param.name, param.slot, param.temp)
        for param in func.params
    ]

    for block, new_block in zip(func.blocks, new_blocks):
        # Non-SSA blocks carry no phis; copy defensively so the result has
        # fully independent containers regardless of input provenance.
        for phi in block.phis:
            new_block.phis.append(
                Phi(
                    phi.dest,
                    {
                        block_map[pred]: value
                        for pred, value in phi.entries.items()
                    },
                )
            )

        for ins in block.instructions:
            if isinstance(ins, Const):
                clone = Const(ins.dest, ins.value)
            elif isinstance(ins, Copy):
                clone = Copy(ins.dest, ins.src)
            elif isinstance(ins, BinOp):
                clone = BinOp(
                    ins.dest, ins.operator, ins.left, ins.right,
                    ins.kind, ins.type,
                )
            elif isinstance(ins, Call):
                clone = Call(ins.dest, ins.name, list(ins.args), ins.type)
            else:
                raise AssertionError(  # pragma: no cover
                    f"unknown instruction: {ins!r}")
            new_block.instructions.append(clone)

        term = block.terminator
        if term is None:
            new_block.terminator = None
        elif isinstance(term, Return):
            new_block.terminator = Return(term.value)
        elif isinstance(term, Jump):
            new_block.terminator = Jump(block_map[term.target])
        elif isinstance(term, Branch):
            new_block.terminator = Branch(
                term.cond,
                block_map[term.true_target],
                block_map[term.false_target],
            )
        else:
            raise AssertionError(  # pragma: no cover
                f"unknown terminator: {term!r}")

    return Function(
        func.name,
        new_params,
        func.ret_type,
        list(func.locals),
        new_blocks,
        block_map[func.entry],
        ssa=False,
    )

"""Pre-refactor snapshots of lowered / SSA / optimized rendering.

Run with cwd = repo root: python3 /tmp/snapshot_ir.py outdir
"""
import sys

sys.path.insert(0, "tests")

from compiler_ir import (
    BinOp, Block, Branch, Call, Const, Copy, Function, Jump, Module,
    Parameter, Phi, Return, Slot, Temp,
    lower_module, optimize_module, render_module, to_ssa,
)
from test_pipeline import (
    arith, assign, bool_, call, compare, func, if_, int_, let, logical,
    param, program, ret, var, while_,
)

AST_PROGRAMS = [
    # diamond (if/else)
    program(func("diamond", [param("c", "bool"), param("x", "int")], "int", [
        let("a", "int", int_(1)),
        if_(var("c"), [assign("a", var("x"))], [assign("a", int_(2))]),
        ret(var("a")),
    ])),
    # missing else
    program(func("noelse", [param("c", "bool"), param("x", "int")], "int", [
        let("a", "int", int_(1)),
        if_(var("c"), [assign("a", var("x"))]),
        ret(var("a")),
    ])),
    # nested branches
    program(func("nested",
                 [param("c", "bool"), param("d", "bool"), param("x", "int")],
                 "int", [
        let("a", "int", int_(0)),
        if_(var("c"),
            [if_(var("d"), [assign("a", var("x"))], [assign("a", int_(9))])],
            [assign("a", int_(7))]),
        ret(var("a")),
    ])),
    # loop with back edges
    program(func("counter", [param("n", "int")], "int", [
        let("acc", "int", int_(0)),
        while_(compare("gt", var("n"), int_(0)), [
            assign("acc", arith("add", var("acc"), var("n"))),
            assign("n", arith("sub", var("n"), int_(1))),
        ]),
        ret(var("acc")),
    ])),
    # nested loop
    program(func("nestedloops", [param("n", "int")], "int", [
        let("i", "int", int_(0)),
        let("s", "int", int_(0)),
        while_(compare("lt", var("i"), var("n")), [
            let("j", "int", int_(0)),
            while_(compare("lt", var("j"), var("n")), [
                assign("s", arith("add", var("s"), int_(1))),
                assign("j", arith("add", var("j"), int_(1))),
            ]),
            assign("i", arith("add", var("i"), int_(1))),
        ]),
        ret(var("s")),
    ])),
    # short-circuit and/or
    program(func("sc", [], "bool", [
        let("r", "bool", logical("and", bool_(True),
                                 compare("eq", int_(1), int_(1)))),
        ret(var("r")),
    ])),
    program(func("scor", [], "bool", [
        ret(logical("or", bool_(False),
                    logical("or", bool_(False), bool_(True)))),
    ])),
    # phi-only cycle loop
    program(func("cycle", [param("n", "int")], "void", [
        let("a", "int", int_(1)),
        let("b", "int", int_(2)),
        while_(compare("gt", var("n"), int_(0)), [
            assign("a", var("b")),
            assign("b", var("a")),
            assign("n", arith("sub", var("n"), int_(1))),
        ]),
    ])),
    # calls
    program(
        func("id", [param("x", "int")], "int", [ret(var("x"))]),
        func("use", [param("a", "int")], "int", [
            let("b", "int", arith("add", call("id", [var("a")]), int_(1))),
            if_(compare("gt", var("b"), int_(0)),
                [ret(var("b"))], [ret(int_(0))]),
        ]),
    ),
    # empty
    program(func("noop", [], "void", [])),
]


def hand_dup_target_branch_module():
    # b0: br cond -> b1, b1 (true and false coincide); b1: return x
    b0 = Block(0)
    b1 = Block(1)
    x = Slot(0, "int")
    t = Temp(0, "bool")
    b0.instructions = [Const(t, True)]
    b0.terminator = Branch(t, b1, b1)
    b1.terminator = Return(x)
    fn = Function("dup", [Parameter("x", x)], "int", [], [b0, b1], b0)
    return Module([fn])


def hand_unreachable_module():
    # b0 return; b1 unreachable with a join shape: jump b2; b2 return;
    # plus an unreachable block that branches to b2 and itself.
    b0 = Block(0)
    b1 = Block(1)
    b2 = Block(2)
    b3 = Block(3)
    v = Slot(0, "int")
    t1 = Temp(0, "int")
    t2 = Temp(1, "int")
    t3 = Temp(2, "bool")
    b0.instructions = [Const(t1, 5)]
    b0.terminator = Return(t1)
    b1.instructions = [Const(t2, 6), Copy(v, t2)]
    b1.terminator = Jump(b2)
    b2.terminator = Return(t1)
    b3.instructions = [Const(t3, False)]
    b3.terminator = Branch(t3, b2, b3)
    fn = Function("unreach", [Parameter("x", v)], "int", [v],
                  [b0, b1, b2, b3], b0)
    return Module([fn])


HAND_MODULES = {
    "dup_target": hand_dup_target_branch_module(),
    "unreachable": hand_unreachable_module(),
}


def main(outdir):
    sections = []
    for i, ast in enumerate(AST_PROGRAMS):
        lowered = lower_module(ast)
        ssa = to_ssa(lowered)
        ssa2 = to_ssa(ssa)
        opt = optimize_module(lowered)
        opt_explicit = optimize_module(lowered, ("ssa", "fold", "dce", "ssa"))
        opt_fold = optimize_module(lowered, ("ssa", "fold"))
        opt_dce = optimize_module(lowered, ("ssa", "dce"))
        opt_empty_nonssa = optimize_module(lowered, ())
        opt_empty_ssa = optimize_module(ssa, ())
        sections.append((
            f"ast_{i}",
            render_module(lowered),
            render_module(ssa),
            render_module(ssa2),
            render_module(opt),
            render_module(opt_explicit),
            render_module(opt_fold),
            render_module(opt_dce),
            render_module(opt_empty_nonssa),
            render_module(opt_empty_ssa),
        ))
    for name, module in HAND_MODULES.items():
        ssa = to_ssa(module)
        sections.append((
            name,
            render_module(module),
            render_module(ssa),
            render_module(to_ssa(ssa)),
            render_module(optimize_module(module)),
            render_module(optimize_module(module, ("ssa", "fold", "dce",
                                                   "ssa"))),
            render_module(optimize_module(module, ("ssa", "fold"))),
            render_module(optimize_module(module, ("ssa", "dce"))),
            render_module(optimize_module(module, ()), ""),
            render_module(optimize_module(ssa, ())),
        ))

    labels = ["lowered", "ssa", "ssa2", "opt", "opt_explicit", "opt_fold",
              "opt_dce", "opt_empty_nonssa", "x", "opt_empty_ssa"]
    for section in sections:
        name = section[0]
        for label, text in zip(labels, section[1:]):
            if label == "x":
                continue
            with open(f"{outdir}/{name}__{label}.txt", "w") as fh:
                fh.write(text)
    print(f"wrote {len(sections)} program snapshots")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main(sys.argv[1])

"""Pre-refactor snapshots of lowered / SSA / optimized rendering.

Run with cwd = repo root: python3 /tmp/snapshot_ir.py outdir
"""
import sys

sys.path.insert(0, "tests")

from compiler_ir import (
    BinOp, Block, Branch, Call, Const, Copy, Function, Jump, Module,
    Parameter, Phi, Return, Slot, Temp,
    lower_module, optimize_module, render_module, to_ssa,
)
from test_pipeline import (
    arith, assign, bool_, call, compare, func, if_, int_, let, logical,
    param, program, ret, var, while_,
)

AST_PROGRAMS = [
    # diamond (if/else)
    program(func("diamond", [param("c", "bool"), param("x", "int")], "int", [
        let("a", "int", int_(1)),
        if_(var("c"), [assign("a", var("x"))], [assign("a", int_(2))]),
        ret(var("a")),
    ])),
    # missing else
    program(func("noelse", [param("c", "bool"), param("x", "int")], "int", [
        let("a", "int", int_(1)),
        if_(var("c"), [assign("a", var("x"))]),
        ret(var("a")),
    ])),
    # nested branches
    program(func("nested",
                 [param("c", "bool"), param("d", "bool"), param("x", "int")],
                 "int", [
        let("a", "int", int_(0)),
        if_(var("c"),
            [if_(var("d"), [assign("a", var("x"))], [assign("a", int_(9))])],
            [assign("a", int_(7))]),
        ret(var("a")),
    ])),
    # loop with back edges
    program(func("counter", [param("n", "int")], "int", [
        let("acc", "int", int_(0)),
        while_(compare("gt", var("n"), int_(0)), [
            assign("acc", arith("add", var("acc"), var("n"))),
            assign("n", arith("sub", var("n"), int_(1))),
        ]),
        ret(var("acc")),
    ])),
    # nested loop
    program(func("nestedloops", [param("n", "int")], "int", [
        let("i", "int", int_(0)),
        let("s", "int", int_(0)),
        while_(compare("lt", var("i"), var("n")), [
            let("j", "int", int_(0)),
            while_(compare("lt", var("j"), var("n")), [
                assign("s", arith("add", var("s"), int_(1))),
                assign("j", arith("add", var("j"), int_(1))),
            ]),
            assign("i", arith("add", var("i"), int_(1))),
        ]),
        ret(var("s")),
    ])),
    # short-circuit and/or
    program(func("sc", [], "bool", [
        let("r", "bool", logical("and", bool_(True),
                                 compare("eq", int_(1), int_(1)))),
        ret(var("r")),
    ])),
    program(func("scor", [], "bool", [
        ret(logical("or", bool_(False),
                    logical("or", bool_(False), bool_(True)))),
    ])),
    # phi-only cycle loop
    program(func("cycle", [param("n", "int")], "void", [
        let("a", "int", int_(1)),
        let("b", "int", int_(2)),
        while_(compare("gt", var("n"), int_(0)), [
            assign("a", var("b")),
            assign("b", var("a")),
            assign("n", arith("sub", var("n"), int_(1))),
        ]),
    ])),
    # calls
    program(
        func("id", [param("x", "int")], "int", [ret(var("x"))]),
        func("use", [param("a", "int")], "int", [
            let("b", "int", arith("add", call("id", [var("a")]), int_(1))),
            if_(compare("gt", var("b"), int_(0)),
                [ret(var("b"))], [ret(int_(0))]),
        ]),
    ),
    # empty
    program(func("noop", [], "void", [])),
]


def hand_dup_target_branch_module():
    # b0: br cond -> b1, b1 (true and false coincide); b1: return x
    b0 = Block(0)
    b1 = Block(1)
    x = Slot(0, "int")
    t = Temp(0, "bool")
    b0.instructions = [Const(t, True)]
    b0.terminator = Branch(t, b1, b1)
    b1.terminator = Return(x)
    fn = Function("dup", [Parameter("x", x)], "int", [], [b0, b1], b0)
    return Module([fn])


def hand_unreachable_module():
    # b0 return; b1 unreachable with a join shape: jump b2; b2 return;
    # plus an unreachable block that branches to b2 and itself.
    b0 = Block(0)
    b1 = Block(1)
    b2 = Block(2)
    b3 = Block(3)
    v = Slot(0, "int")
    t1 = Temp(0, "int")
    t2 = Temp(1, "int")
    t3 = Temp(2, "bool")
    b0.instructions = [Const(t1, 5)]
    b0.terminator = Return(t1)
    b1.instructions = [Const(t2, 6), Copy(v, t2)]
    b1.terminator = Jump(b2)
    b2.terminator = Return(t1)
    b3.instructions = [Const(t3, False)]
    b3.terminator = Branch(t3, b2, b3)
    fn = Function("unreach", [Parameter("x", v)], "int", [v],
                  [b0, b1, b2, b3], b0)
    return Module([fn])


HAND_MODULES = {
    "dup_target": hand_dup_target_branch_module(),
    "unreachable": hand_unreachable_module(),
}


def main(outdir):
    sections = []
    for i, ast in enumerate(AST_PROGRAMS):
        lowered = lower_module(ast)
        ssa = to_ssa(lowered)
        ssa2 = to_ssa(ssa)
        opt = optimize_module(lowered)
        opt_explicit = optimize_module(lowered, ("ssa", "fold", "dce", "ssa"))
        opt_fold = optimize_module(lowered, ("ssa", "fold"))
        opt_dce = optimize_module(lowered, ("ssa", "dce"))
        opt_empty_nonssa = optimize_module(lowered, ())
        opt_empty_ssa = optimize_module(ssa, ())
        sections.append((
            f"ast_{i}",
            render_module(lowered),
            render_module(ssa),
            render_module(ssa2),
            render_module(opt),
            render_module(opt_explicit),
            render_module(opt_fold),
            render_module(opt_dce),
            render_module(opt_empty_nonssa),
            render_module(opt_empty_ssa),
        ))
    for name, module in HAND_MODULES.items():
        ssa = to_ssa(module)
        sections.append((
            name,
            render_module(module),
            render_module(ssa),
            render_module(to_ssa(ssa)),
            render_module(optimize_module(module)),
            render_module(optimize_module(module, ("ssa", "fold", "dce",
                                                   "ssa"))),
            render_module(optimize_module(module, ("ssa", "fold"))),
            render_module(optimize_module(module, ("ssa", "dce"))),
            render_module(optimize_module(module, ())),
            render_module(optimize_module(ssa, ())),
        ))

    labels = ["lowered", "ssa", "ssa2", "opt", "opt_explicit", "opt_fold",
              "opt_dce", "opt_empty_nonssa", "opt_empty_ssa"]
    for section in sections:
        name = section[0]
        for label, text in zip(labels, section[1:]):
            with open(f"{outdir}/{name}__{label}.txt", "w") as fh:
                fh.write(text)
    print(f"wrote {len(sections)} program snapshots")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main(sys.argv[1])

"""Internal control-flow analysis layer.

This module is the single home of the CFG computations shared by SSA
construction and later control-flow-aware optimizations:

* successor edges in fixed terminator order (a branch whose true and false
  edge hit the same block yields one successor, not two);
* predecessors restricted to edges between reachable blocks;
* the reachable block set together with a stable function-order listing;
* a reverse postorder numbering;
* immediate dominators (the entry dominates itself);
* dominator-tree children;
* dominance frontiers.

Every result is keyed by the original :class:`~compiler_ir.ir_nodes.Block`
objects of the analyzed function; the function is never mutated.  Blocks
unreachable from the entry stay in :attr:`ControlFlowAnalysis.blocks` (and
retain their outgoing successors) but never appear in the reverse
postorder, the dominator tree, the dominance frontiers, or in any reachable
block's predecessor list.

All list-valued results use an order derived from function block order or
from fixed terminator edge order -- never from set iteration, object
identity or hashing -- so repeated analyses are observationally identical.

The layer is internal: it is not an optimization pass and is not part of
the package's public exports.
"""
from .ir_nodes import Block, Branch, Function, Jump


class ControlFlowAnalysis:
    """Block-keyed control-flow relations for one :class:`Function`.

    Attributes
    ----------
    blocks:
        The function's blocks in function (label) order.
    index:
        Mapping of every block to its position in :attr:`blocks`.
    succs:
        Every block's successor blocks in fixed terminator edge order
        (jump target, then branch true/false targets), with a repeated
        branch target collapsed to a single entry.
    preds:
        Predecessor blocks, in function block order, counting only edges
        whose source and target are both reachable.  Unreachable blocks
        have an empty list.
    reachable:
        Set of blocks reachable from the entry.
    reachable_order:
        The same blocks as :attr:`reachable`, listed in function order.
    rpo:
        Reachable blocks in reverse postorder of the successor DFS.
    idom:
        Immediate dominator of every reachable block; the entry maps to
        itself.
    children:
        Dominator-tree children of every reachable block, sorted by block
        index.
    frontiers:
        Dominance frontier of every reachable block, sorted by block index.
    """

    __slots__ = (
        "blocks", "index", "succs", "preds", "reachable", "reachable_order",
        "rpo", "idom", "children", "frontiers",
    )

    def __init__(
        self,
        blocks: list[Block],
        index: dict[Block, int],
        succs: dict[Block, list[Block]],
        preds: dict[Block, list[Block]],
        reachable: set[Block],
        reachable_order: list[Block],
        rpo: list[Block],
        idom: dict[Block, Block],
        children: dict[Block, list[Block]],
        frontiers: dict[Block, list[Block]],
    ):
        self.blocks = blocks
        self.index = index
        self.succs = succs
        self.preds = preds
        self.reachable = reachable
        self.reachable_order = reachable_order
        self.rpo = rpo
        self.idom = idom
        self.children = children
        self.frontiers = frontiers

    def sort(self, blocks) -> list[Block]:
        """Sort blocks by their stable function block index."""
        return sorted(blocks, key=lambda b: self.index[b])


def analyze_function(func: Function) -> ControlFlowAnalysis:
    """Compute all control-flow relations of ``func`` without mutating it."""
    blocks = list(func.blocks)
    index = {block: i for i, block in enumerate(blocks)}

    succs: dict[Block, list[Block]] = {
        block: _terminator_edges(block) for block in blocks
    }

    entry = func.entry
    reachable = _reachable_set(succs, entry)
    reachable_order = [b for b in blocks if b in reachable]

    preds: dict[Block, list[Block]] = {block: [] for block in blocks}
    # Walking the blocks in function order keeps every predecessor list in
    # a deterministic order independent of set iteration.  Only edges
    # between reachable blocks count, so an unreachable source never shows
    # up and an edge into an unreachable island is ignored.
    for block in blocks:
        if block not in reachable:
            continue
        for target in succs[block]:
            if target in reachable:
                preds[target].append(block)

    rpo = _reverse_postorder(succs, reachable, entry)
    idom = _immediate_dominators(rpo, preds)
    children = _dominator_children(reachable_order, idom, entry, index)
    frontiers = _dominance_frontiers(reachable_order, preds, idom, index)

    return ControlFlowAnalysis(
        blocks=blocks,
        index=index,
        succs=succs,
        preds=preds,
        reachable=reachable,
        reachable_order=reachable_order,
        rpo=rpo,
        idom=idom,
        children=children,
        frontiers=frontiers,
    )


# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Individual relation computations
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------


def _terminator_edges(block: Block) -> list[Block]:
    """Successors of ``block`` in fixed edge order, without duplicates.

    A conditional branch whose true and false targets coincide is one CFG
    edge: the target appears once, so it can never gain a repeated
    predecessor or duplicated dominance information downstream.
    """
    term = block.terminator
    if isinstance(term, Jump):
        return [term.target]
    if isinstance(term, Branch):
        if term.true_target is term.false_target:
            return [term.true_target]
        return [term.true_target, term.false_target]
    return []


def _reachable_set(
    succs: dict[Block, list[Block]], entry: Block
) -> set[Block]:
    seen = {entry}
    stack = [entry]
    while stack:
        block = stack.pop()
        for target in succs[block]:
            if target not in seen:
                seen.add(target)
                stack.append(target)
    return seen


def _reverse_postorder(
    succs: dict[Block, list[Block]],
    reachable: set[Block],
    entry: Block,
) -> list[Block]:
    """Reverse postorder of an iterative successor DFS.

    Successors are expanded in fixed edge order, which (together with the
    edge-order deduplication in :func:`_terminator_edges`) makes the
    result independent of hashing.
    """
    order: list[Block] = []
    visited = {entry}
    stack = [(entry, 0)]
    while stack:
        block, pos = stack[-1]
        successors = succs[block]
        if pos < len(successors):
            stack[-1] = (block, pos + 1)
            target = successors[pos]
            if target in reachable and target not in visited:
                visited.add(target)
                stack.append((target, 0))
        else:
            order.append(block)
            stack.pop()
    order.reverse()
    return order


def _immediate_dominators(
    rpo: list[Block], preds: dict[Block, list[Block]]
) -> dict[Block, Block]:
    """Immediate dominators (Cooper-Harvey-Waterman iterative fix point).

    The entry's immediate dominator is the entry itself.  Predecessors are
    consulted in function block order, so the initial candidate and each
    intersection step are free of set-iteration effects.
    """
    rpo_index = {block: i for i, block in enumerate(rpo)}
    preds_order = {
        block: [p for p in preds[block] if p in rpo_index] for block in rpo
    }

    def intersect(a: Block, b: Block) -> Block:
        while a is not b:
            while rpo_index[a] > rpo_index[b]:
                a = idom[a]
            while rpo_index[b] > rpo_index[a]:
                b = idom[b]
        return a

    idom: dict[Block, Block] = {rpo[0]: rpo[0]}
    changed = True
    while changed:
        changed = False
        for block in rpo[1:]:
            new_idom = next(p for p in preds_order[block] if p in idom)
            for pred in preds_order[block]:
                if pred is new_idom or pred not in idom:
                    continue
                new_idom = intersect(pred, new_idom)
            if idom.get(block) is not new_idom:
                idom[block] = new_idom
                changed = True
    return idom


def _dominator_children(
    reachable_order: list[Block],
    idom: dict[Block, Block],
    entry: Block,
    index: dict[Block, int],
) -> dict[Block, list[Block]]:
    children: dict[Block, list[Block]] = {
        block: [] for block in reachable_order
    }
    for block in reachable_order:
        if block is not entry:
            children[idom[block]].append(block)
    for child_list in children.values():
        child_list.sort(key=lambda b: index[b])
    return children


def _dominance_frontiers(
    reachable_order: list[Block],
    preds: dict[Block, list[Block]],
    idom: dict[Block, Block],
    index: dict[Block, int],
) -> dict[Block, list[Block]]:
    """Cytron-style dominance frontiers (their Figure 5 loop)."""
    frontiers: dict[Block, list[Block]] = {
        block: [] for block in reachable_order
    }
    for block in reachable_order:
        if len(preds[block]) < 2:
            continue
        for pred in preds[block]:
            runner = pred
            while runner is not idom[block]:
                frontiers[runner].append(block)
                runner = idom[runner]
    for nodes in frontiers.values():
        nodes.sort(key=lambda b: index[b])
    return frontiers

"""Internal control-flow analysis layer.

This module is the single home of the CFG computations shared by SSA
construction and later control-flow-aware optimizations:

* successor edges in fixed terminator order (a branch whose true and false
  edge hit the same block yields one successor, not two);
* predecessors restricted to edges between reachable blocks;
* the reachable block set together with a stable function-order listing;
* a reverse postorder numbering;
* immediate dominators (the entry dominates itself);
* dominator-tree children;
* dominance frontiers.

Every result is keyed by the original :class:`~compiler_ir.ir_nodes.Block`
objects of the analyzed function; the function is never mutated.  Blocks
unreachable from the entry stay in :attr:`ControlFlowAnalysis.blocks` (and
retain their outgoing successors) but never appear in the reverse
postorder, the dominator tree, the dominance frontiers, or in any reachable
block's predecessor list.

All list-valued results use an order derived from function block order or
from fixed terminator edge order -- never from set iteration, object
identity or hashing -- so repeated analyses are observationally identical.

The layer is internal: it is not an optimization pass and is not part of
the package's public exports.
"""
from .ir_nodes import Block, Branch, Function, Jump


class ControlFlowAnalysis:
    """Block-keyed control-flow relations for one :class:`Function`.

    Attributes
    ----------
    blocks:
        The function's blocks in function (label) order.
    index:
        Mapping of every block to its position in :attr:`blocks`.
    succs:
        Every block's successor blocks in fixed terminator edge order
        (jump target, then branch true/false targets), with a repeated
        branch target collapsed to a single entry.
    preds:
        Predecessor blocks, in function block order, counting only edges
        whose source and target are both reachable.  Unreachable blocks
        have an empty list.
    reachable:
        Set of blocks reachable from the entry.
    reachable_order:
        The same blocks as :attr:`reachable`, listed in function order.
    rpo:
        Reachable blocks in reverse postorder of the successor DFS.
    idom:
        Immediate dominator of every reachable block; the entry maps to
        itself.
    children:
        Dominator-tree children of every reachable block, sorted by block
        index.
    frontiers:
        Dominance frontier of every reachable block, sorted by block index.
    """

    __slots__ = (
        "blocks", "index", "succs", "preds", "reachable", "reachable_order",
        "rpo", "idom", "children", "frontiers",
    )

    def __init__(
        self,
        blocks: list[Block],
        index: dict[Block, int],
        succs: dict[Block, list[Block]],
        preds: dict[Block, list[Block]],
        reachable: set[Block],
        reachable_order: list[Block],
        rpo: list[Block],
        idom: dict[Block, Block],
        children: dict[Block, list[Block]],
        frontiers: dict[Block, list[Block]],
    ):
        self.blocks = blocks
        self.index = index
        self.succs = succs
        self.preds = preds
        self.reachable = reachable
        self.reachable_order = reachable_order
        self.rpo = rpo
        self.idom = idom
        self.children = children
        self.frontiers = frontiers

    def sort(self, blocks) -> list[Block]:
        """Sort blocks by their stable function block index."""
        return sorted(blocks, key=lambda b: self.index[b])


def analyze_function(func: Function) -> ControlFlowAnalysis:
    """Compute all control-flow relations of ``func`` without mutating it."""
    blocks = list(func.blocks)
    index = {block: i for i, block in enumerate(blocks)}

    succs: dict[Block, list[Block]] = {
        block: _terminator_edges(block) for block in blocks
    }

    entry = func.entry
    reachable = _reachable_set(succs, entry)
    reachable_order = [b for b in blocks if b in reachable]

    preds: dict[Block, list[Block]] = {block: [] for block in blocks}
    # Walking the blocks in function order keeps every predecessor list in
    # a deterministic order independent of set iteration.  Only edges
    # between reachable blocks count, so an unreachable source never shows
    # up and an edge into an unreachable island is ignored.
    for block in blocks:
        if block not in reachable:
            continue
        for target in succs[block]:
            if target in reachable:
                preds[target].append(block)

    rpo = _reverse_postorder(succs, reachable, entry)
    idom = _immediate_dominators(rpo, preds)
    children = _dominator_children(reachable_order, idom, entry, index)
    frontiers = _dominance_frontiers(reachable_order, preds, idom, index)

    return ControlFlowAnalysis(
        blocks=blocks,
        index=index,
        succs=succs,
        preds=preds,
        reachable=reachable,
        reachable_order=reachable_order,
        rpo=rpo,
        idom=idom,
        children=children,
        frontiers=frontiers,
    )


# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Individual relation computations
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------


def _terminator_edges(block: Block) -> list[Block]:
    """Successors of ``block`` in fixed edge order, without duplicates.

    A conditional branch whose true and false targets coincide is one CFG
    edge: the target appears once, so it can never gain a repeated
    predecessor or duplicated dominance information downstream.
    """
    term = block.terminator
    if isinstance(term, Jump):
        return [term.target]
    if isinstance(term, Branch):
        if term.true_target is term.false_target:
            return [term.true_target]
        return [term.true_target, term.false_target]
    return []


def _reachable_set(
    succs: dict[Block, list[Block]], entry: Block
) -> set[Block]:
    seen = {entry}
    stack = [entry]
    while stack:
        block = stack.pop()
        for target in succs[block]:
            if target not in seen:
                seen.add(target)
                stack.append(target)
    return seen


def _reverse_postorder(
    succs: dict[Block, list[Block]],
    reachable: set[Block],
    entry: Block,
) -> list[Block]:
    """Reverse postorder of an iterative successor DFS.

    Successors are expanded in fixed edge order, which (together with the
    edge-order deduplication in :func:`_terminator_edges`) makes the
    result independent of hashing.
    """
    order: list[Block] = []
    visited = {entry}
    stack = [(entry, 0)]
    while stack:
        block, pos = stack[-1]
        successors = succs[block]
        if pos < len(successors):
            stack[-1] = (block, pos + 1)
            target = successors[pos]
            if target in reachable and target not in visited:
                visited.add(target)
                stack.append((target, 0))
        else:
            order.append(block)
            stack.pop()
    order.reverse()
    return order


def _immediate_dominators(
    rpo: list[Block], preds: dict[Block, list[Block]]
) -> dict[Block, Block]:
    """Immediate dominators (Cooper-Harvey-Waterman iterative fix point).

    The entry's immediate dominator is the entry itself.  Predecessors are
    consulted in function block order, so the initial candidate and each
    intersection step are free of set-iteration effects.
    """
    rpo_index = {block: i for i, block in enumerate(rpo)}
    preds_order = {
        block: [p for p in preds[block] if p in rpo_index] for block in rpo
    }

    def intersect(a: Block, b: Block) -> Block:
        while a is not b:
            while rpo_index[a] > rpo_index[b]:
                a = idom[a]
            while rpo_index[b] > rpo_index[a]:
                b = idom[b]
        return a

    idom: dict[Block, Block] = {rpo[0]: rpo[0]}
    changed = True
    while changed:
        changed = False
        for block in rpo[1:]:
            new_idom = next(p for p in preds_order[block] if p in idom)
            for pred in preds_order[block]:
                if pred is new_idom or pred not in idom:
                    continue
                new_idom = intersect(pred, new_idom)
            if idom.get(block) is not new_idom:
                idom[block] = new_idom
                changed = True
    return idom


def _dominator_children(
    reachable_order: list[Block],
    idom: dict[Block, Block],
    entry: Block,
    index: dict[Block, int],
) -> dict[Block, list[Block]]:
    children: dict[Block, list[Block]] = {
        block: [] for block in reachable_order
    }
    for block in reachable_order:
        if block is not entry:
            children[idom[block]].append(block)
    for child_list in children.values():
        child_list.sort(key=lambda b: index[b])
    return children


def _dominance_frontiers(
    reachable_order: list[Block],
    preds: dict[Block, list[Block]],
    idom: dict[Block, Block],
    index: dict[Block, int],
) -> dict[Block, list[Block]]:
    """Cytron-style dominance frontiers (their Figure 5 loop)."""
    frontiers: dict[Block, list[Block]] = {
        block: [] for block in reachable_order
    }
    for block in reachable_order:
        if len(preds[block]) < 2:
            continue
        for pred in preds[block]:
            runner = pred
            while runner is not idom[block]:
                frontiers[runner].append(block)
                runner = idom[runner]
    for nodes in frontiers.values():
        nodes.sort(key=lambda b: index[b])
    return frontiers
